name: Vehicle Maintenance
description: Keep every household vehicle road-legal and maintained: a service log with costs and odometer readings, plus annual renewal reminders for registration, inspection, and insurance.

vehicles.sql: SELECT id, name, make_model, model_year, plate, notes, archived, created_by, created_at FROM app_vehicle_maintenance__vehicles WHERE archived = 0 ORDER BY created_at

service_log.sql: SELECT id, vehicle_id, service_date, title, odometer, cost_cents, notes, created_by, created_at FROM app_vehicle_maintenance__service_log ORDER BY service_date DESC LIMIT 500

renewals.sql: SELECT id, vehicle_id, member_id, kind, title, event_month, event_day, lead_days, visibility, notes, last_reminded_at, created_at, updated_at FROM app_vehicle_maintenance__renewals

suggested_automations.title: Put every vehicle renewal on the household calendar
suggested_automations.description: When a registration, inspection, or insurance renewal is added or its date is changed, put an all-day calendar event on the reminder day — two weeks before it is due, by default. The renewal list here stores only a month and a day; this projects the next actual date so it shows up in the month view and in the calendar feed the household already subscribes to. Editing the date moves the entry that is already there instead of adding a second one.

suggested_automations.title: Take a vehicle renewal back off the calendar
suggested_automations.description: The other half of the rule above, and it does nothing without it. When a renewal is deleted, or the vehicle it belongs to is archived, the calendar entry it put there stops showing — instead of standing for years as a registration for a car the household no longer owns. Add both, or the entry outlives the vehicle.

source.query: SELECT id AS id, title AS title, kind AS subtitle, member_id AS member_id, :today AS when_at FROM app_vehicle_maintenance__renewals WHERE event_month = CAST(strftime('%m', :today) AS INTEGER) AND event_day = CAST(strftime('%d', :today) AS INTEGER) LIMIT 20

SELECT title AS title, kind AS subtitle, member_id AS member_id, CASE WHEN printf('%02d-%02d', event_month, event_day) >= substr(:today, 6, 5) THEN printf('%04d-%02d-%02d', CAST(substr(:today, 1, 4) AS INTEGER), event_month, event_day) ELSE printf('%04d-%02d-%02d', CAST(substr(:today, 1, 4) AS INTEGER) + 1, event_month, event_day) END AS at FROM app_vehicle_maintenance__renewals ORDER BY at LIMIT 3
